items.title: 56422_Leonard Phillips oral history interview
items.q: John got this job at the Dykes, and then he took six pieces out there. He took me

ctx.x: So then he got this gig in...

Yeah. He got one out in Dykes Stockade. When that one was over, John got this job at the Dykes, and then he took six pieces out there. He took me, he took Cragbrains and Curtis, and Tommy Potter on bass...
This was when he took them from 26th Street to the other gig. Is that what you're saying?

items.title: 68089_John Malachi oral history interview
items.q: when I had the little band with Charlie Rouse and Phil Phillips and Osie Johnson and Tommy Potter and Harry Curtis

ctx.x: But Art Tatum went through a lot of things like that, playing all sorts of lousy pianos and everything. And he never seemed to complain at all. A lot of times you didn't know how lousy the piano was until you sat down and tried to play it yourself! Then you realized that it was just something different about the way he did it, that you didn't notice these things when he was playing.

I guess that's probably wrapped up in the piano learnings in Washington from those people that I mentioned.... During the time that I was down at the Crystal Caverns, when I had the little band with Charlie Rouse and Phil Phillips and Osie Johnson and Tommy Potter and Harry Curtis... This was 1942. We were playing one night. And the shows from the Howard Theatre would always come down after the last show, and have

drinks or have something to eat, or come down just to catch the show and the music. And a lot of times the fellows would come and sit in with us. Once I remember Walter Page coming down and sitting in with us, and some of the other musicians who I don't remember...
